proposals.title: Listen to one article
proposals.trigger: The user has opened an article from Home and wants to keep up with the story while away from the screen.
proposals.userNeed: Hear this article without having to read it. Completing an ad could grant one playback of this article.
proposals.eligibility: Readers of an article for which narration and playback rights are available; exclude anyone who already has the feature through a paid entitlement.
proposals.productChange: Add an optional Listen control on the article screen and single-article narration. Neither the control nor an ad-funded grant was observed.
proposals.reward: One playback of the current article, not ongoing audio access.
proposals.optIn: Tapping Listen opens a choice to watch a rewarded ad; playback starts only after the user affirmatively chooses it and the ad completes.
proposals.fulfillment: Enable playback for the current article and return the user to that article.
proposals.declinePath: Close the offer and continue reading normally.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, do not grant playback; return to the readable article with a non-ad retry option where appropriate.
proposals.businessImpact: Could add ad revenue and listening utility, but narration and rights may cost money. It must not replace normal reading or a paid audio benefit; if a relevant purchase offer is introduced, show that path first and consider an ad sample only after it is declined.
proposals.validationPlan: Run a single-article audio experiment measuring completed listens, article engagement, ad yield, narration costs, and any change in paid conversion against a no-offer group.
assumptions: Article narration and its rights can be provided; grantability and per-play cost are unknown.
No plan price or paid audio entitlement was observed; subscription overlap and business metrics are unknown.

proposals.title: Listen to this article once
proposals.trigger: While reading an article opened from Home, the user wants to continue the story without looking at the screen.
proposals.userNeed: Hear the current article when reading is inconvenient; a completed ad could unlock one playback.
proposals.eligibility: Readers of articles with confirmed narration rights. Exclude users whose verified paid entitlement already includes this playback.
proposals.productChange: Add narration and an optional Listen control to eligible articles. Neither audio nor an ad-funded grant was observed. Check actual paid entitlements before launch; if a relevant purchase offer applies, keep it first and show the ad option only after the reader leaves it.
proposals.reward: One playback of the current article, not full-access or ongoing audio access.
proposals.optIn: The proposed Listen control explains the one-playback reward. Playback requires an affirmative choice to watch an ad and a completed ad.
proposals.fulfillment: Unlock playback for the current article and keep the reader on that article.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the offer and continue reading normally; do not change any existing purchase offer.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, grant nothing and return to the readable article. Offer a retry only when an ad becomes available.
proposals.businessImpact: Audio may improve article use and earn ad revenue, but narration, rights, and delivery may cost money. The offer must not restrict free reading or displace a paid benefit. The observed Telegraph full-access prompt does not establish an audio entitlement or its terms.
proposals.validationPlan: First confirm rights, per-play costs, reader interest, and actual paid entitlements. Then test eligible-article Listen access against no offer, measuring opt-ins, completed listens, reading engagement, net ad yield after costs, and any change in subscription conversion.
assumptions: Narration rights and a one-playback grant are technically and contractually possible; availability and costs are unknown.
Audio demand, ad yield, plan prices, paid audio benefits, and effects on subscription conversion are unknown.

proposals.title: One Home news briefing
proposals.trigger: The user is scanning Home's news stories and wants a quick overview before choosing what to read.
proposals.userNeed: Get a concise briefing of several currently shown stories after an ad, while retaining the ability to open any story normally.
proposals.eligibility: Home readers when enough eligible stories are available to assemble a briefing; exclude users who already receive an equivalent paid benefit.
proposals.productChange: Add an optional Briefing control on Home that compiles attributed highlights with links to the underlying articles. Briefings and ad-funded grants were not observed.
proposals.reward: One briefing of the current Home stories, not unlimited briefings or access to articles.
proposals.optIn: The user taps Briefing, then explicitly chooses to watch a rewarded ad before generation begins.
proposals.fulfillment: After a completed ad, show the briefing on Home with links to the ordinary article flow.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the offer and keep browsing or opening articles as before.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, do not generate the rewarded briefing; leave the Home feed usable.
proposals.businessImpact: Could help readers discover stories and earn ad revenue, but generation, attribution, and publisher permissions may add costs. It must not reduce the existing free feed or displace a paid benefit; any future relevant purchase path should be offered first.
proposals.validationPlan: Test the Home briefing against the unchanged feed, tracking article opens, reading time, ad yield, generation costs, and paid conversion.
assumptions: A useful, rights-compliant briefing can be assembled from eligible stories; grantability and cost are unknown.
No plan price or paid briefing entitlement was observed; subscription effects and business metrics are unknown.

proposals.title: One Home news briefing
proposals.trigger: A reader is scanning several Home stories and wants to decide which article to open.
proposals.userNeed: Get a quick overview of eligible stories without losing the normal article-opening path.
proposals.eligibility: Home readers when enough stories have permission for attributed summaries. Exclude anyone with an equivalent paid entitlement; check for relevant paid benefits before launch.
proposals.productChange: Add an optional Briefing control on Home. It would assemble short, attributed highlights from permitted stories, each linking to its article. Neither briefings nor ad-funded grants were observed.
proposals.reward: One briefing of the currently eligible Home stories after a completed ad; no article access or recurring briefing allowance.
proposals.optIn: Tapping Briefing opens an offer that states the one-briefing reward; generation starts only if the reader affirmatively chooses to watch the ad.
proposals.fulfillment: After ad completion, display the briefing on Home with links into the ordinary article flow.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the offer and continue browsing or opening stories normally.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, grant no briefing and return to the usable Home feed.
proposals.businessImpact: May improve story discovery and produce ad yield, but could replace article opens or incur rights, generation, and serving costs. Preserve the free feed. No paid briefing benefit was observed; if a relevant paid offer exists, present that purchase path first and assess whether this one-use reward would undercut it.
proposals.validationPlan: First verify publisher permissions, attribution, and reader usefulness. Then A/B test the optional briefing against the unchanged Home feed, measuring article opens, reading time, ad yield, costs, and any applicable paid conversion; stop or revise if it displaces reading or paid uptake.
assumptions: Rights-compliant summaries can be made from enough Home stories; grantability and unit costs are unknown.
No plan pricing or paid briefing entitlement was observed. Applicable paid benefits and effects on subscriptions, normal reading, and business metrics require verification.
